justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.2.1 requires a data specification validated as consistent and complete for intended use, functionally aligning with Art 10(1). Gap: ISO 5259 is sector-neutral and does not specifically address high-risk AI systems under regulatory oversight.
gap: ISO 5259-3 does not reference the high-risk AI regulatory classification or the specific quality criteria in Art 10(2)-(5).

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.3.1 requires a DQ plan covering processes throughout the data life cycle, supporting Art 10(1). Gap: ISO does not require the plan to demonstrate compliance with a regulation.
gap: The DQ plan is not required to reference regulatory compliance or demonstrate that datasets satisfy a legal standard.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.2.2 requires specifying dataset design parameters, partially covering Art 10(2)(a) design choices. Gap: Art 10(2)(a) includes AI model and algorithm design choices beyond dataset format specification.
gap: AI model architecture and algorithm selection — the AI system design choices sense — are outside ISO 5259 scope.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.4.2 requires taking into account licensing and reuse conditions, partially covering data origin. Gap: ISO does not require documenting provenance at the individual-collection-purpose level for personal data.
gap: Provenance of personal data at the individual collection purpose level is not addressed by ISO 5259-3.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.4.3 requires documenting reasons for collection, method and specification, covering collection processes and origin. Gap: ISO does not require the original purpose of personal data collection (GDPR framing).
gap: The original purpose of personal data collection as a GDPR-grounded requirement is not addressed by ISO 5259-3.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.5.2 comprehensively covers data cleaning operations. Gap: Art 10(2)(c) requires documentation of annotation and labelling processes, which ISO 5259-3 does not explicitly mandate.
gap: Annotation and labelling as formally documented data-preparation operations are not explicitly required by ISO 5259-3.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.2.3 requires specifying statistical properties and representativeness, implicitly addressing what data represents. Gap: ISO does not require explicitly documenting measurement assumptions as a distinct governance obligation.
gap: Explicit documentation of measurement assumptions (what the data is supposed to measure and represent) is not a distinct ISO 5259-3 requirement.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.1.1(a) requires documenting the motivation and origin of the data need, partially covering Art 10(2)(e). Gap: ISO does not require a formal prior assessment of availability, quantity and suitability before data acquisition.
gap: A formal documented assessment of dataset availability, quantity and suitability before acquisition is not explicitly required by ISO 5259-3.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.5.2(d) requires bias and drift detection/mitigation measures. Gap: Art 10(2)(f) frames bias examination around health, safety, fundamental rights and anti-discrimination — legal-rights framing structurally absent from ISO 5259.
gap: Fundamental rights and anti-discrimination framing of bias examination is outside ISO 5259 scope.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §8.3.4 requires risk assessment covering data quality risks including bias. Gap: ISO risk management does not address risks to fundamental rights or anti-discrimination under Union law.
gap: ISO 5259-3 risk management does not address risks to fundamental rights or discrimination under Union law.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §8.3.4 requires identifying and mitigating data quality risks, functionally covering data gap identification. Gap: Art 10(2)(g/h) requires explicitly documenting gaps and HOW they will be addressed as a governance obligation.
gap: The gap-documentation obligation (document gaps and the plan to address them) as a distinct governance item is not explicit in ISO 5259-3.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.2.3 covers statistical properties per subset. Gap: ISO does not specifically require properties to account for the specific persons/groups the AI system is used on.
gap: The fairness/demographic dimension — statistical properties adequate for specific persons/groups the AI system is used on — is absent from ISO 5259-3.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.1.1(b) requires specifying scope and intended use, implicitly encompassing deployment setting. Gap: ISO does not explicitly require characterising geographical, behavioural or functional deployment context as distinct quality parameters.
gap: Explicit characterisation of geographical, contextual, behavioural and functional deployment setting is not required by ISO 5259-3.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.8.3 requires deletion from all storage locations. Gap: ISO does not tie deletion to the legal trigger (bias corrected OR retention period ended).
gap: The legal deletion trigger — bias corrected OR retention period ended — is not addressed by ISO 5259-3.

justification: ISO 5259-3 §7.3.2.3 covers subset specification including test data. Gap: ISO has no scoping provision limiting requirements to testing datasets only for non-training AI systems.
gap: No ISO 5259-3 provision scopes requirements to testing datasets only for non-training AI systems.
